label: EXPERIMENTAL snowpack-structure prediction for expert decision support. Not an avalanche forecast, danger rating or operational guidance.
source: Avalanche Canada Mountain Information Network (public reports)

reports.title: Sunshine Backcountry
reports.comment: quick: We skied south, east and west aspects on Mt Standish. The height of snow at tree line is about 40 cm.  If you stick to the deepest part of mellow slopes you can avoid hitting any rocks.  Trail break was a lot of work.  The mid pack was quite facetted and the snow skied quite slow.  Below tree line there isn't much snow.  Areas that had a bit of wind slab underneath skied better. 10 minute l…

reports.title: Wawa Hump
reports.comment: quick: Did one run on the east aspect of the wawa hump above the lift.  Warm tempatures and lots of wind and new snow made for poor skiing.   Extensive cracking and some whumping above the lift.  Foot penetration was to ground.  I dug a quick pit at 2400m on east aspect. I found multiple generations of wind slab over faceted base and a decomposing rain crust on the ground.  The 10 cm 1 finger wind…

reports.title: Monarch
reports.comment:
quick: Snow was soft, no cracking or whumpfing. Nothing spooky. 
First turns of the year, kept it mellow and safe

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment:
quick: Rain crust evident to 2100m elevation, around 30-50cm good powder above that.
Avalanche conditions prime with no issues below treeline as that's all we rode today (nothing steep and no crazy terrain).

reports.title: Size 1.5 Avalanche
reports.comment: quick: While skinning along the top of a wind loaded slope with a wind lip/cornice shooting cracks remotely triggered and released the slope below. 70cm crown approximately 25m wide released the slope which ran 50m to a runout zone below and stopped.

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: Plenty of fresh snow on Healy Pass, deep powder in the trees and in areas sheltered from the wind, I wouldn't look to do anything in the alpine anytime soon as it looked very wind affected. / snowpack: Completed a compression test with results on 3 different layers. Layer at 80cm and at 65cm both had sudden planer fractures at 4 & then 10 taps, we then triggered a layer at 45cm which was a …

reports.title: Sunshine meadows+
reports.comment:
quick: Some of the best skiing of the season inbounds and in the Backcountry this season.  The storm last night finished with no wind.  Through the warm tempatures made for slow cakey snow on the flats. 

When the sun came out this morning it triggered loose dry avalanches above bourgeau left hand  that almost went over the ice climb, see picture.  

Ski patrol triggered two size 2+ avalanches in …

reports.title: Bourgeau Left
reports.comment: quick: The first pitch of Bourgeau Left is gone. Lots of snow around too and a big pile of wet debris in the gully below the route. Bourgeau Right looks almost formed, but the first pitch looks hard. Also very snowy.

reports.title: SSV slack
reports.comment: quick: Good turns up high above 2200m in at least 15cm of unconsolidated pow. Pit at 2350m E aspect had HS 165cm and ECTX which was quite surprising as we were expecting something on the Nov interfaces. On the way down BTL, good turns quickly turned to dust on crust circa 2050 to Armageddon lower down (re frozen tree bombs, frozen runnels, lots of new deadfall, etc). Was also surprised not to see …

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: Ventured up to Healy Pass today. Travel was challenging off of the skin track until around the Simpson Pass turnoff with the rain crust prevalent to 2200m ish. Beyond this, the crust turned supportive and by the time we were in the sub alpine, there was 25cm of fresh on top. A few quick hand pits showed this no reactivity between this layer and the crust below however we chose to ski mellow…

reports.title: Wawa Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Wawa Ridge to Wawa Bowl under Repeater Slopes. Ridge line was unexposed with reasonable coverage up to below Repeater Slopes. Rocky sections above to top of Wawa. Lots of failed cornices with no reaction. Probe of snowpack shows now layers or crust, but over all dense. No slab or reactions from skiing. / snowpack: Consistent, consolidated snow pack. Probing showed no crusts. No storm slabs …

reports.title: Sunshine Ski Area Profile
reports.comment: quick: Sunshine snow profile. Generally a supportive snowpack with a well settled mid-pack.  The main concerning layer is the November 5th Facet/crust interface at the bottom of the snowpack. You can find more details on this deep persistent weak layer in the avalanche bulletin for Banff, Kootenay, Yoho and Little Yoho.

reports.title: Dinosaur head
reports.comment: quick: Skied into dinosaur head from the resort. Some wind loading taking place but seemingly unreactive when tested on steep convexitys. Rain crust was evident when we got lower down with 5cm or less overlying it. Lot more coverage than expected in the trees and pillows!

reports.title: Healy pass
reports.comment:
quick: Heavy trail breaking at TL and ALP up to healy pass. In wind pressed powder. The tele hagans gave a good workout today. Uptrack just past the Simpson pass turnoff gets a bit messy for a brief moment to avoid downed trees. 

HS 125cm at 2350m in wind exposed SE slope. 55cms on top of early December interface. No crust. F to 4F density in top 55cms, CTH 21 RP on this interface. No surface cra…

reports.title: Twin Cairns
reports.comment: quick: There are lots of exposed rocks and lots of rock under a thin layer of snow so watch out. Uptrack I noticed whumpfing in wind loaded areas. No shooting cracks. Rode the riders left face, facing east. Rode a more concave path and stuck to the trees. For the conditions and terrain it was a more challenging line but there are plenty of simple lines that have lots of untouched powder on the Nor…

reports.title: Healy Creek to Sunshine
reports.comment: quick: Stayed on all mellow slopes. No signs of instability throughout ascent, heard one large avalanche in the valley, couldn’t tell where it came from. Multiple hand shear tests showed slabs breaking around 30cm deep on average.

reports.title: Ice - SRU
reports.comment:
quick: **Did a wee bit of saw work on the approach to avoid a limbo move.  
**Ice is a big tube and as you reach the top you can see down into the tube through a couple holes. Quite a cavern in there.  
**Front of the tube is wet and building outwards but needs to thicken a bit.  
**Despite the tube being thinner as you get higher, thicker ice can be had to the sides, even taking 16's in spots. So…

reports.title: Mt Bourgeau avalanche control
reports.comment: quick: Avalanche control above the Sunshine Village access road today. We threw 11 large explosives into 4 different avalanche paths and only got small, surface soft slabs 15 cm deep up to size 1.5.

reports.title: Goats Eye
reports.comment: quick: Went to check out goats eye today. We had some minor cracking while skining. The storm snow wasn’t bonded very well with the crust below it. It was a fairly thin snowpack near the creek (50-60cms), at 2000m there was 180cm. On the dissent we skied onto a steep shoulder in the slide path and had a skier trigger a small slide (0.5-1) that propagated a few meters in front of them. / weather: P…

reports.title: Quartz Ridge/Hill reconnaissance
reports.comment: quick: Lowering cloud cover, reduced visibility and flat light on the ridgeline prevented us from skiing the main N/NE faces. From the flats a size 1 natural, cornice 10m wide, 60m long on the upper slope of quartz hill was visible before reduced visibility allowed a closer look. Appeared on the leeward side of the main SW winds. Snow coverage on ridgetop was soft with light wind slab forming from…

reports.title: Bourgeau Meadows
reports.comment: quick: Evidence of significant wind in the area recently, though it was not windy on Sunday when we were up there. Pit at 2400m NE aspect, CTE3 RP down 20cm, CTH23 RP down 80cm, HS 250cm. Saw a Sz1 natural slab on east casing wind loaded slope that looked to be about 20-30cm crown, 15m across, may have been cornice triggered. No other signs of instability. Ski quality was great in sheltered areas.

reports.title: Goats Eye
reports.comment:
quick: Poked around up to goats eye. HS was 120 at 2000m.
Lots of wind travel up at the eye and most of the snow in the alpine had been wind scoured. We decided to only go up to the obvious strip of trees at tree line. Started hearing whomping at 1910. After some more loud whomps we decided the mountain didn’t want us up there and we backed off. Skiing down you could feel the snow starting to stif…

reports.title: Bourgeau Left - Avalanche over the climb
reports.comment: avalanche: Small natural avalanche started near the top of Mt Bourgeau and snaked is way down and over the Bourgeau Left ice climb within the last 12hrs +/-. Debris stopped at the base of the route.

reports.title: Wawa Bowl / Wizard Chutes
reports.comment: quick: Did lap down wawa bowl and wizard chutes. Significant wind affect at ridgeline, but good skiing in sheltered areas. No obvious signs of instability. Hand shear tests showed smaller reactive pockets of windslab and a CT at 2400m SE aspect wind loaded slope produced no significant results. Found  facets down 80cm, but did not produce results.

reports.title: Twin Carins Scenic Walk
reports.comment:
quick: Mellow skin up Twin Carins. Best skiing was 5cm loose snow down W facing slope from Standish towards Carins. 
Wind scoured and firm for skin up Twin Carins and for ski down low-angle NNW slope from top. / snowpack: CT in N-facing thick wind roll at base of twin Carins. 24 deg. No result.

reports.title: Loose dry avalanches in alpine
reports.comment: quick: We saw 3 size 1 dry loose avalanches start on east aspects in the alpine. None stepped down into deeper layers. No evidence of avalanches on west aspects. Low wind in the trees until about 1pm but lots of wind transport in the alpine.

reports.title: Healy Creek Avalanche Paths
reports.comment:
quick: Skied the looker’s far right Healy creek avalanche path. Minimal wind on the ascent with patchy clouds, became windy once we gained the ridge line.

Snow was mostly good with patches of wind scoured crust. While descending other party member triggered 1-1.5 slab avalanche with a run out of 100-200m. No one was caught in the avalanche and it was allowed to run its course.

reports.title: Rock Isle Lake
reports.comment:
quick: Toured around Rock Isle Lake, a small 30m wide slide triggered by a cornice fell on the leeward side of this face of approx 45 degrees, revealed a 40cm deep fracture. Snow was otherwise stable on low angle slopes. 
Great snow in areas not affected by wind. Lots of snow being transported in to leeward slopes with multiple buried cross loaded slabs in the alpine.

reports.title: Touchy new cornices around SSV slack
reports.comment: quick: Surprisingly touchy cornices on Wawa ridge as we were heading up … they were stepping back much more than usual and were quite significant. Didn’t trigger any slabs although I’d be leery of anything in the alpine and would take a cautious approach with them until they firm up.

reports.title: Sightings from Wawa
reports.comment:
avalanche: Debris/crown was spotted from a distance while lapping Wawa Ridge. 

Mt Bourgeau: Size 1.5 coming off a steep, SE slope dotted with cliffs into the drainage where it continued to travel ≈100m. 

Mt Brett South Bowl: Size ≈3 also coming off a steep SE planar slope. Crown line visible from afar.

reports.title: Twin Cairns
reports.comment: quick: Skied Twin Cairns today. Snow wind affected but softer than expected in places with some dust on crust and less sastrugi than Kananaskis Sunday. One avalanche (size 1?) observed off of steep rocky terrain on a lee aspect of the Monarch.

reports.title: Harvey Pass/Mt Bourgeau
reports.comment:
quick: There was enough new snow to make skiing pleasant between 2100m and 2400m on south aspects..  Not much snow in the Alpine on west and SW slopes.  The sun came out briefly mid-afternoon and took the snow surface to 0C just below treeline.. 

Our uptrack didn't find the easy terrain and we got cliffted out once on descent.

At the end of the day it got warm down low with snow balling and stic…

reports.title: Big V - Healy creek - SSV slack
reports.comment: quick: Hit the big V today along Healy after trying (unsuccessfully) to rip out a big chunk of cornice while on belay to test slope stability. Cornice was rock hard and not going anywhere even though it was gigantic. Big V itself skied wonderfully - boot top to knee deep. Some minor wind skin (3cm or so) but no other significant obs from the day. Basically Rogers Pass conditions close to home ...

reports.title: Massive west facing slidepath
reports.comment: quick: Went out to Massive pass and the west facing slopes. On the skin in we noticed some size 1s in the Avi paths on Pilot mountain in the steeper terrain likely from a day or two ago. We opted to ski the west Avi paths over the pass as it looked less wind affected. On our uptrack we weren't happy with the feeling of support of the snow on the drought crust. Decided not to continue into the stee…

reports.title: Mount Bourgeau
reports.comment: quick: Skied and scrambled Mount Bourgeau yesterday (Feb 25) via Bourgeau Lake. The lower skin track was icy but 10-15cm of powder was found above the switchbacks where signs of foot travel petered out. The terrain above the lake was larger than I anticipated but manageable with no signs of instability. Some soft wind slabs were found overlaying hard wind crusts and could be suspect with future lo…

reports.title: Cory Pass
reports.comment: quick: Long skin to Cory Pass ended after we dug a pit and decided to ultimately not ski into the pass. Top layer (new powder on crust) failed at CT15 and lower layer had a really clean planar failure at CT25. Pit was in the shade on north facing slope, tons of sun on other slopes and the amount of natural avalanches (although small) didnt give anyone a good feeling.

reports.title: Twin Cairns Approach
reports.comment: quick: No result from a CT. 30 degree, Northern facing slope, depth 180cm,elevation 2444m. Crust layers 20cm and 40cm from top.

reports.title: Pilot mountain east facing chutes
reports.comment:
quick: Recent naturals on nearly all the chutes starting above treeline. Rode below treeline and was stable. Some sluffing from upper cliffs. Would need to manage sluff on tight, steep zones.
Overall amazing run

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment:
avalanche: Several point releases with wide runout on both avy paths en route to Healy pass. Not directly observed, but more added from in to out time. / snowpack: Feb crust down about 20cm on S aspect at 2200m. Not observed on N aspect at same elevation. Lots of settlement cones. 
Surface snow was light at 11, heavy by 1pm.

reports.title: Healy Pass Peak
reports.comment: quick: Skied Healy Pass Peak today. Skinned up the S Ridge which is quite wind affected but has sufficient coverage but would be a marginal ski. Boot packed the last 20m or so. Down climbed the NE ridge a short ways before dropping down to ski the SE face. Snow was generally agreeable with a firm base, some sharks present. Returned via Healy Pass Trail. A cold west wind prevelant at ridgetop, snow…

reports.title: Bourgeau Niner
reports.comment:
quick: Bourgue lake and surrounding bowls on the up track showed very little signs of any recent snow instability or fetch transport. Recent snow with lighter winds recently has provided great coverage to the ridge with F-4F snow on-top of an old supportive crust layer. 

Skied Bourgeau 9. On entry Sc Sz 1 on wind loaded convexity propagated 10m Wide adjacent and below the skier, ran 30m pulling 5…

reports.title: Massive mountain
reports.comment: quick: We skied NWW slopes off Massive, we skied it just as the sun started to hit the slope. It skied super well, there was some slab that propagated on the east aspect of the ridge when skinning up, pretty minor. We skied the north east bowl after off the col. It had a little bit of wind effect but still skied nicely. Saw some small sluffs come down with the warming on the slopes, likely tree bo…

reports.title: Twin Cairns
reports.comment: quick: Triggered 0.25 Avalanche from wind slab over facets on solid wind slab. 10m x 10m x 3-10cm. / avalanche: Skier triggered 0.25 avalanche; 10m x 10m  x 3-10cm. Skier moved 3-5m without loosing balance. Triggered immediately from entry below small cornice. No action required to arrest. Small windslab on facets just above hard and stable wind affected slope. Small (2m x 2m x 3cm) windslab was e…

reports.title: Massive Southern Gully
reports.comment: avalanche: Thin soft slab to ground initiated after traversing under upper face to start southern gully. / incident: Thin soft/wind slab to ground triggered near start of southern most gully on Massive.

reports.title: Monarch Unskiable Terrain Avalanche
reports.comment: quick: Day time highs reached -3. Top level of snowpack only barely being affected by temps, little direct sun. / avalanche: Avalanche observed from a distance. Occurred in steep unskiable terrain. / snowpack: Compression test resulted in no failure.

reports.title: Healy Area
reports.comment: quick: Good skiing up Healy but anything even slightly south facing has a bit of a sun crust under 5 to 10 cm of new storm snow.  It's easy to break through and wasn't as bad as we were expecting but worth considering on steep terrain where the new snow has bonded poorly and is easy to get moving in a sluff.  Did a hand sheer and found a moderate resistant planar layer down 40 cm.  No action on th…

reports.title: Bourgeau ice fall loose wet
reports.comment: quick: Bourgeau went again today - really big loose wet that we witnessed from the parking lot at 2:40 and lasted at least 2 minutes …

reports.title: Goat's Eye
reports.comment: avalanche: Starting from the top of the goats eye, we noticed a small 1meter Crack that came off the skis. We decided to do a small ski cut which resulted in a touchy 10 meter wind slab propagation off the skis, and running about 100m down through the choke. We knocked off the remaining debris in chunks, then proceeded to have some great turns down the face. / weather: Light blowing snow at tge to…

reports.title: Bourgeau Meadows
reports.comment: quick: Did some mellow riding in Bourgeau Meadows. -10 in the parking lot, up to -5 in the alpine around noon.  Freeze thaw conditions on the uptrack. Snow improved greatly at about 2100m with 10cm on top of a thin solar crust. Good riding on North facing aspects. Solar aspects were hammered by the sun and turned into a slushy mess. Bourgeau had noticeable activity on the south face in the alpine,…

reports.title: Spray River Falls
reports.comment:
quick: Climbed Spray River Falls today and chose it because it faces north and the day was forecast to be cool and cloudy. Approach was frozen trail and when we neared the climb there was a few cm of dry snow on the crust.

Large piles of avalanche debris in the gully leading to the climb which came from old, wet avalanches off the lookers right side gully walls. Impressive piles.

The sun came ou…

reports.title: Quartz ridge, Sunshine Meadows
reports.comment: quick: Sportive melt freeze crust with 3-4 cm of wind pressed snow on top made for good skiing and travel in the sunshine meadows.  Skied the NE aspect off Quartz ridge, no crust felt.  Low angle solar aspects skied well to. Steep solar aspects had variable crust especially if it had been skied before and were unpleasant. Cornices were growing and wind slabs in certain features. No melt today exce…

reports.title: Twin Cairns North Aspect
reports.comment: quick: Conditions Matched Forecast. Snow was stable on N/W Aspects.  Wind affected on N Slopes but was still ok skiing. Cornices present above West aspect along ridgeline. Snow was ok.

reports.title: Cornice near SSV
reports.comment: quick: Cool day but still saw this fresh cornice failure.

reports.title: Ice - Bearspirit
reports.comment:
quick: **Approach is mostly snow free although icy in spots. The approach ice step is losing ice and in part has water over rock. Despite that two hikers still managed to get up it.
**Left side has a tricky but fun slot.
**Middle has a bit of a wet line left, then a dry groove, and a featured steep line right. The upper half also seemed to have more fracturing.  
**Right side had a good groove alt…

reports.title: Eagle Mountain/The Goat's Eye
reports.comment:
quick: Went much of the way up Eagle Mountain towards the Goat's Eye on Sunday. -8 at the car starting around 8am and mixed sun/clouds. A storm did roll in starting around noon, cloud cover and snow was pretty consistent after that.

Overall, conditions lined up pretty well with the forecast. Shortly after we went from treeline to alpine there was wide spread windslab that was pretty poorly bonded…

reports.title: Cornice failure
reports.comment: quick: Just a reminder of Spring cornice failures. Failure occurred within the last 2 days on the route to Quartz in Sunshine backcountry.

reports.title: Quartz Ridge
reports.comment: quick: I skied and boot packed to the summit of Quaztz ridge. Wet sluffs to size 1.5 off the steep east face of the Monarch began around 1015 am due to intense solar radiation. On the north ridge I encounter thigh deep facets. The main summit has 10 cm wind slab over facets. We avoided the big roll over on the summit.  I would recommend waiting a few melt freeze cycles before skiing from the summi…

reports.title: Bye Bye
reports.comment: quick: There is a good crust on solar aspects that provides good travel and good crust skiing. I also had good corn skiing on the south aspects after 1200.   The Sunshine area didn't get as much snow as kananaskis did, so is making for better corn skiing.  Tomorrow looks hot and sunny and I expect loose wet cycle to start mid to early afternoon depending on the wind.  The crust held up right to th…
